## Reporting a bug - [x] I am using the latest ~~released~~ master version of Numba (most recent is visible in the change log (https://github.com/numba/numba/blob/master/CHANGE_LOG). - [x] I have included below a minimal working reproducer (if you are unsure how to write one see http://matthewrocklin.com/blog/work/2018/02/28/minimal-bug-reports). Looks like output dtype is incorrect when an operation has array and scalar inputs (see below). This happens for both integer and float types, and seems different than the [integer typing semantic issue](https://numba.pydata.org/numba-doc/dev/proposals/integer-typing.html). np.testing functions don't seem to check for dtype matching, so this is easy to miss. I came across this issue since pd.testing functions do check for dtype matching. ```python In [36]: A = np.arange(5, dtype=np.int32) In [37]: numba.njit(lambda A: A+1)(A).dtype Out[37]: dtype('int64') In [38]: (A+1).dtype Out[38]: dtype('int32') ```
